newsitem.title: UK: Europe debt futures to rest then rush on-chartists.
newsitem.headline: Europe debt futures to rest then rush on-chartists.

text.p: Sizzling European bond futures are ripe for a consolidation after soaring to record highs, but technical analysts said on Friday there are more gains to come.

Technical analysts, who eschew economic fundamentals in favour of price action, say Italian and French debt futures will continue to be supported by Bunds which recently cracked an important chart level.
"We are probably reaching a point of exhaustion which will encourage consolidation," said Tom Hobson, director of technical analysis at Merrill Lynch in London.
"But it's not a reason to go short, it's more a reason to pare back a little on long positions," he said.
He said the rallies had been supported by big increases in open interest.
"That means the market has a sentiment and vulnerability to the upside. People have to come in and buy these markets and that will underpin any type of pull back," Hobson said.
High-yielding markets have fared particularly well.

"The most spectacular of the regular markets is BTPs," said Adrian Sells, director of Crane Investment Analysis. "Any indicator will show the market is overbought but good markets can remain so for some time without worrying about it."

"It could correct quite radically back to 118.00, that's not impossible," he said. "But only a break below the 117.00 area would signal a downtrend. Barring that, there's no reason not to look for a further push on into the 120s."
Shea Bennett, technical analyst at Trend Analysis agreed a correction was in store.
"It has all been very flash in pan. We'll probably see profit-taking over the next few days," he said.

December BTP futures were at 121.90 by 1231 GMT, up a whopping 147 basis points, having climbed to a new all-time high at 122.50 earlier in the session. The market has jumped a full eight points since the beginning of September, shattering the previous all-time high of 119.15 set in February 1994.
"Medium term BTPs are still bullish and there is nothing really to change that at the moment," Bennett said, adding the picture was the same for the other major European bond markets.

Hobson said the European markets were well supported by Bunds which had recently broken through an important resistance level at 98.30. This was the high on March 8 before U.S. payroll data sent the market diving.
"It's the most important technical development of the last few days," he said.
On weekly continuation charts this level was the first of two significant break points in the 1996 Bund sell off.
The second was a gap between 99.34 and 99.46, he said. This area has yet to be broken. At 1244 GMT, December Bund futures were at 98.90, up five basis points on the day.
"The number one thing that will guide these markets and indicates a consistently positive tone in Europe, is that Bunds are going to make a move towards that gap," said Hobson.
"That will support the other markets. All of Europe has now assumed a more positive directional bias," he said.
Chartists set a medium term target for Bunds of 100.00 to 100.50, with some saying once the contract reached par, a test of the 101.36 high from January 26 would quickly follow.

December notionnel futures were slightly more vulnerable in the short-term, said Bennett. But the contract would push up to a new contract high at 125.40 before correcting to around 122.70 and from there climbing to 127.00, he said.
At 1245 GMT, December notionnel futures were at 125.02, up 24 basis points from Thursday's close.
Sells said while the notionnel had performed strongly in recent weeks, it was still a long way off its record high. On continuation charts the notionnel reached a high at 131.38 on January 16, 1994.
"Nevertheless it's put in a strong performance. In the bigger picture there is a good chance it will continue to make eventual progress towards 130/131 area on a continuation futures basis," he said.
